title: Antigone (This Play I Read In High School) by Anna Ziegler at The Pub...
transcript: Antigone is one of the most well known tragic heroines, yet we're still finding new ways to know her. The conflict of the original Sophocles play is largely over a man's body, with Antigone's principles guiding her defiance to Creon. In this surprisingly fresh take on the story by Anna Ziegler, currently running at The Public, it's Antigone's body that causes conflict. Creon is the one guided by principles, though they're flawed and no match for Antigone's convictions. In an era where women's rights are perpetually at stake, this play makes a scorching case on how laws, though theoretical for the mostly men making them, have real consequences for the people governed by them. With knockout performances from the entire cast, this production viscerally illustrates how ownership and agency are inextricably linked, regardless of what the law says. I enjoyed this play quite a bit despite its occasionally flawed execution. There's a framing device where a narrator functions as both an outside commentator and a character whose point of view somewhat modernizes the story. The balance between these roles isn't quite right and sometimes the plot explanations and provided context come at the expense of digging deeper into the story's personal relevance to the narrator. I also found some of the scenes dragging longer than was necessary to serve their purpose, but I wasn't complaining about getting more stage time with folks like Tony Shalhoub, Susannah Perkins, Celia Keenan-Bolger, and Calvin Leon Smith — truly a stacked set of actors, all of whom get meaty assignments. With that, another Playbill for my collection.
